::: {.project-facts}
**Role:** circuit builder and Python programmer

**Inputs:** pedestrian request switch

**Outputs:** red, yellow, and green indicators
:::

## The problem

Create a traffic-light sequence that never displays conflicting vehicle states.
A pedestrian request is remembered and served at a safe transition rather than
changing outputs immediately.

## State model

Document each state, permitted next state, output pattern, duration, and response
to a request. Run the same state logic on a keyboard-driven simulator before
connecting external LEDs.

## Software test evidence

| Test | Expected | Synthetic result |
|---|---|---|
| normal cycle | green → yellow → red | pass |
| request during green | stored until transition | pass |
| repeated request | one pending request | pass |
| shutdown | all external outputs off | pass |

## Circuit verification

For each LED, show the actual GPIO level, LED forward-voltage assumption,
current-limiting resistor calculation, measured voltage, and safe shutdown test.

## Mistake and revision

The first version used blocking delays, so a request could be missed. I revised
the program to check elapsed time and input events while maintaining the current
state.

## Conclusion

Software tests support the sequencing rules, while voltage measurements support
the physical interface. Neither form of evidence replaces the other.
